sloka: Who, indeed, that is highly capable in achieving seen and unseen goals, will not be adorned by this praśnottararatnamālikā when it is worn on the neck?

Memorizing the Prashnottara Ratnamālika is like wearing an ornament made of precious gems around the neck. Teachings in it help a person achieve goals that are worldly (इह)  as well as those beyond this world. (पर)
1. Oh Divine One (Guru)! What must be accepted? Guru's instructions.
2. What must be rejected? Forbidden action; Action that should not be done
3. Who is a Guru? One who has realized the tattva, the everlasting and unchanging Truth;  Who is ever striving for the welfare of the śiṣya, disciple.
upādeyam (उपादेयम्) - That which is worthy of acceptance
heyam (हेयम्) - That which must be abandoned, rejected, or given up
4. What must be done by the wise with utmost urgency? Severance of the cyclic chain of birth and death, saṃsāra
5. What is the seed for the tree of liberation, mokṣa (release from saṃsāra)? Knowledge obtained by performing ordained actions and duties.
It is emphasized that mere theoritical or textbook knowledge is not enough. To bear fruit, tt must be practiced and lived through by performing ordained duties everyday.
6. What is most beneficial?  dharma.
7. Who is pure in this world? One whose mind is clean.
8. Who is a pandita (wise person)? One who is discerning; One who discriminates between permanent (nitya), and ephemeral (anitya).
9. What is harmful like poison? Disrespect toward Gurus.
avadhīraṇā (अवधीरणा) - contempt, disrespect, disregard, treating with slight.
10. What is the essence of samsara?  This alone must be reflected upon repeatedly. (and realize that there is no essence in samsara)
11. What is the most desirable amongst men? A life which is beneficial to self and others.
iṣṭatamaṃ (इष्टतमम्)- Most desirable, most cherished
12. What causes delusion like alcohol? Attachment such as to wealth, children, etc.
13. Who are the real thieves? Objects of the senses.
14. What grows like a creeper? Extreme desire.
15. Who is the real enemy? Lack of effort, laziness.
dasyavaḥ (दस्यवः) - Thieves, robbers, plunderers
anudyogaḥ (अनुद्योगः) - lack of effort, laziness, indolence
16. What causes fear? Death.
17. Who is even blinder than a physically blind person? One with worldly passions and attachments.
18. Who is a true hero? One who is not disturbed by the piercing glances of women.
It implies a hero is one who has overcome sensory temptations.
19. What is the nectar that is fit to be drunk by the ears that are like cupped hands? Good advice.
20. What causes respectability? Not asking for anything, non-soliciting.
21. What is completely unfathomable? Conduct of women.
22. Who is truly clever? One who has not succumbed to the above.
23. What is true misery? Discontentment.
24. What causes a loss of dignity? Begging or soliciting from an ignoble person.
25. What is true living? A flawless life lived with purity and integrity.
26. What is stupidity? Not putting into practice what has been learnt.
27. Who is truly awake? One who is discerning; one who can distinguish between what is permanent and what is ephemeral.
28. What is real sleep? Ignorance (to the purpose of life) of living beings.
29. What is as fleeting like a water droplet on a lotus petal? Youth, wealth, and life itself.
30. Who are universally pleasant like the moonlight? Saints, noblemen, and gentlemen - those who are always pure, moral, and righteous in their conduct.
31. What is hell? Subjugation (dependence on others)
32. What is true happiness? Detachment from all worldly associations.
33. What is the ultimate goal to be achieved? Welfare of all living beings.
34. What is most dear to living beings? Life itself
35. What results in ruin? Arrogance or Egoistic pride
36. What bestows happiness? Friendship with the virtuous.
37. Who is adept at destroying all calamities? A renunciate (One who has renounced everything)
38. What is equivalent to death? Stupidity.
39. What is priceless? Timely help.
40. What hurts like a thorn until death? A misdeed committed in secrecy.
41. Where should one put his efforts? Acquiring knowledge, right medicine, and charity.
42. What should be held in contempt? Wicked people, other's women, and other's wealth.
43. What should be contemplated day and night? The lack of essence in worldly things, not an enchanting woman (implying not worldly pleasures).
44. What should be cherished (nurtured)? Compassion for the helpless and friendship with the righteous.
45. Whose mind can never be reformed, even on the brink of death? A fool, a suspicious person, a despondent person, and an ungrateful person.
46. Who is a virtuous person? One whose conduct is righteous.
47. Who is considered base? One whose conduct is unrighteous.
48. Who has conquered the world? A person endowed with truth and forbearance.
titikṣā  (तितिक्षा) - Forbearance, patience in the face of hardships.
49. Who do the gods bow to? One who is foremost in compassion.

50. What causes anguish in the wise? The forest-like world of saṃsāra (which, while beautiful to look at, poses a multitude of dangers where it is easy to lose one's way and fail to reach the final destination).
51. Who holds natural influence over all creatures? One who speaks truth pleasantly and is humble.
52. Where should one choose to abide? On the righteous path, that bestows both earthly and spiritual rewards.
53. Who is blind? One who is engrossed in unrighteousness.
54. Who is deaf? One who doesn't heed beneficial advice.
55. Who is dumb? A person who doesn't speak pleasantly when needed.
56. What is true charity? Giving without expectation.
57. Who is a true friend? One who restrains you from wrongdoing.
58. What is a true ornament? Good character.
59. What embellishes speech? Truth.
60. What is as fleeting as lightning? The company of the wicked and young women.
61. Who remain unshaken in their character even in the age of Kali? The virtuous alone.
62. What is as difficult to obtain in this world as the wish-fulfilling Chintamani gem? The four-fold virtues termed as Chaturbhadram.
63. What do the wise, who have dispelled all ignorance, explain that (Chaturbhadram) further?
63. t is charity paired with sweet words, knowledge devoid of pride, courage tempered with forgiveness, and wealth combined with renunciation.
64. What is pitiable? Miserliness despite possessing wealth.
65. What is praiseworthy? Generosity.
66. Who is revered by the wise? One who is naturally humble at all times.
67. Who brings happiness and glory to their entire family? One who remains humble despite possessing an abundance of virtues.
68. Who holds sway over the entire world? One whose speech is kind and truthful, and who is ever anchored in dharma, righteousness.
69. What captivates the minds of the learned? Sublime poetry and enlightened knowledge.
70. Whom does calamity never touch? One who acts according to the counsel of wise elders and maintains mastery over the senses.
71. Whom does prosperity (Goddess Lakshmi) favor? One who is industrious and lives ethically.
72. Whom does she (Goddess Lakshmi) abandon abruptly? One who has contempt for the wise, teachers, and deities, or is completely lazy.
73. Where should one choose to reside? In the company of the virtuous, or in the holy city of Kashi.
74. Which place should one completely avoid? A place with slanderers; ruled by a greedy king.
75. By virtue of what factors is a man not needing to be lamented over? A devoted spouse and steady wealth.
76. Who in this world is truly needing to be lamented over? One who does not give despite possessing abundant wealth.
77. What causes humiliation? Begging favors from unrefined and lowly people.
78. Who is braver even than Lord Rama? One who is not perturbed by Manmatha’s arrows (which give rise to desires).
79. What should be contemplated day and night? The feet of the Lord, and not the world
80. Who are blind despite having eyes? Atheists.
81. Who is lame in this world? One who goes on a pilgrimage in old age
82. What is the ultimate pilgrimage? That which removes the impurities of the mind.
